source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

31061.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Franklin County stayed overwhelmingly with Republican Pete Ricketts, who beat independent Dan Osborn 948 to 191, a 62-point margin. That is 8 points narrower than Donald Trump's 70-point win in 2024. Every Nebraska county moved toward Osborn, but Franklin moved less than most, ranking 89th of 93. The typical county shifted 14 points, as did the state. Similar counties nearby moved further: Harlan by 11 points, Garden by 12 and Furnas by 14.

Turnout fell sharply, from 1,600 votes in 2024 to 1,222, or 76% of the earlier total. The count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

31133.t:
Pawnee County voted for Pete Ricketts over independent Dan Osborn in the U.S. Senate race, 744 to 326, a Republican margin of 36 points. That is 22 points narrower than Trump's 58-point margin there in 2024, a bigger swing away from the Republican than the state's 14 points and the fifth-largest of Nebraska's 93 counties, all of which moved the same way. Similar small counties shifted less: Sherman by 17 points, Nance by 16, Dixon by 10.

Turnout was 1,148 votes, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Similar counties moved about as much: Gage 18 points, Cass 16 and Adams 15.

About 6,476 votes were cast, 79% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Only 2,739 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

The typical county moved 14 points, matching the statewide swing. Similar counties moved less: Kearney 11 points, Butler 13 and Fillmore 15.

Turnout fell to 3,591 votes, 73% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell people who changed their minds apart from people who stayed home.
